key_insight: Vorticity-dependent convective feedback can generate shielded cyclones and persistent vortex crystals resembling Jupiter’s polar configuration.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a simplified framework for studying how localized convective forcing organizes large-scale rotating flows.
method: Simulate polar dynamics with a γ-plane shallow-water model.
Represent convection as localized impulsive mass sinks, more likely in cyclonic regions.
Use a Biot–Savart diagnostic to separate vortex and background contributions to structural drift.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments reproduce persistent vortex crystals and show that stronger mesoscale feedback promotes vortex growth, shielding, and spectral organization.
watch_item: Vortex scale depends on both deformation radius and convective parameterization, so quantitative predictions require careful parameter sensitivity assessment.
paper_title: Jovian Polar Vortex Generation in a Shallow-Water Model with Quasi-Stochastic Convection
